title: Book Two · Chapter 60: The Paper Boat Race
story:
On Wednesday, rain keeps the children inside during break. Jun finds three small scraps of used paper. One side of each is blank.

“Boats?” he asks.

Ronan looks at the wet window. “There is no river here.”

“Good. We can stay dry.”

They ask Miss Wu for a shallow tray. She gives them an empty one, but no water. They must keep the desks dry too.

Jun puts the tray on the floor. The boys fold their scraps into little boats. Ronan makes a wide bottom. Leo folds the front into a sharp point. Jun's boat leans to one side.

“How do they move?” Ronan asks.

Jun blows. His boat falls over.

“That one needs a better wind,” Leo says.

They straighten it. Ronan blows next. His boat slides across the tray and touches the far edge. He lifts both hands.

“First!”

“Mine has not started,” Leo says.

They put all three boats at the same end. Ronan wants to blow hard again. Jun points to his face.

“Same place for your mouth.”

They choose a line in the floor. Each boy must sit behind it. Each boat gets one breath. Mei comes over to watch. She agrees to move the boats back.

Leo's sharp boat goes far, but turns sideways. Jun's boat travels only halfway. Ronan takes a deep breath. The front of his wide boat lifts. The boat rolls over. It stops beside Jun's.

Mei presses her lips together. Then she laughs.

“Your boat flies.”

“It was a strong wind,” Ronan says.

“Too strong,” Jun says.

They try one more round. Ronan uses a gentler breath. This time his boat reaches the far end. Leo's goes a little farther across the flat floor of the tray. Jun's boat stays upright and moves straight.

They each choose a different boat as the best.

Mei asks to try Jun's boat. Jun moves aside and gives her his place.

She sits behind the same line. First she puts her face too close to the tray.

“The line,” Leo says.

“I know. I am looking at the boat.”

She sits back again. Her first breath only moves it a little. She laughs and tries to pull more air in.

“One breath,” Ronan says.

“That was mine.”

She leaves the boat where it stopped. Then she gives it back to Jun.

“It stayed up.”

Jun looks pleased. He straightens the little front edge.

Ronan puts his own boat beside it. His boat has a much wider bottom. He feels the folded paper with one finger, but he does not open it. He wants to take the boat home in its present shape.

Mei gets up from the floor. She brushes dust from her knees before she returns to the three boats. Mei puts one at each end and the third in the middle.

“A whole boat family,” she says.

At the bell, the tray goes back empty. They leave the boats on dry paper near the window. The boats stay there until school ends. Ronan takes his own home.

He puts it beside the wooden boat for a moment. The wooden boat has green paint at both ends now. It is much heavier. He does not blow at it.

Dad sees the paper boat at supper and asks about the race. Ronan makes it turn over with one short breath.

“This was my first try,” he says.

Dad sets it upright. “Give it a smaller storm next time.”
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

race＝比赛；dry＝干的；fold＝折叠。

## 理解问题

1. 三个孩子怎样让纸船试验公平？
2. Ronan的船最后怎样了？

## 读句子

**Jun / puts / the tray on the floor.** Jun／把托盘／放在地上。
